_comment: The file your marker generator should write beside every image it makes.
One entry per generated board, keyed by the name you give the image — that
same name is what Fusion keeps when you insert it as a decal, so the key
survives the trip through the CAD and nothing has to be encoded in the
The split: this file owns WHAT the marker is (dictionary, ids, metric
size). Fusion owns WHERE it is (pose, host face, planarity). Neither side
can produce a usable marker alone, which is why the join exists.
entity_token is Fusion's own persistent id. It is not known until the
decal has been inserted once, so leave it out of the generator's output
and let the exporter fill it in — after that a rename cannot break the
link. Matching by name still works, and warns that it did.
image_px is not decoration. With the physical extent it is the only way
to see a non-uniform scale, which turns square markers into rectangles
that the pose solver still treats as squares.
The two boards below are the real ones from create_grid_board.ipynb and
dummy_bam_fb_macro.xacro, with the id ranges FIXED — the shipped version
gives all four L2 faces ids 0-4, so a detector cannot tell them apart.

forearm_L2_top._note: 1.5in tube: marker ~= 0.7 x 38.1, then separation = margin = (38.1 - 27.1)/2 = 5.5, which makes the outer width equal the tube width exactly

upperarm_L1_top._note: 2in tube, specified in create_grid_board.ipynb but never wired into the xacro
